newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Foreigners still far below Taiwan stock ceiling.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners still far below Taiwan stock ceiling.

text.p: Foreign investors have remitted US$11.069 billion into Taiwan's stock market, leaving room for US$80.348 billion more before an official ceiling is hit, the central bank said on Tuesday.
As of March 8, foreign investors could invest up to $91.417 billion in the stock market under rules capping foreign holdings at 25 percent of the bourse's market value, the bank said in a statement.
In September 1996, the bank raised the ceiling to 25 percent from 20 percent and allowed foreign individuals to trade Taiwan stocks.
In February, foreign funds remittance into the stock market totalled US$1.310 billion, up from US$739 million in January, the statement said.
A total of US$983 million of such funds flowed out of Taiwan in February, up from January's US$443 million.
February's net remittance was US$327 million, compared to US$296 million in January.
Taiwan's stock market has seen frantic turnover in recent months during a long bull run that has added more than 1,400 points to the local benchmark index in 1997.
The stock market gained 559.93 points in February and 371.32 to date in March.
Foreigners remitted a net total of US$159 million from March 1 to 8, the central bank statement said.
Aside from direct stock holdings, the bank has approved an inflow of US$1.66 billion for funds raised overseas by local firms through convertible bonds and global depositary receipts.
In this category, foreigners as of March 8 had remitted US$537 million into Taiwan and could send US$1.123 billion more before reaching a legal ceiling, the bank said.
